methods.note: The text on pp. 15-16 supports HotSpot as a four-layer RC network (die, spreader, sink, convective layer) solved with 4th-order Runge-Kutta. The extraction also says the same solver gives a steady-state result for Fig. 6, but the survey never states that, so that claim is unsupported. Fig. 6 is an illustrative schematic and not a reproducible experiment.

code.note: The packet lists no assets and the paper links no repositories (checked_no_links). No code, solver version or script was verified. Calling the setup a 2D reproduction would need a later repo default or an inferred HotSpot configuration, and neither counts as evidence.

parameters.note: The 0.8 K/W convection resistance and 45 C ambient on p. 16 are general HotSpot or original-validation values, not stated for Fig. 6. No die, spreader, TIM or sink dimensions, no material properties, no block coordinates or sizes, and no power-to-block mapping are given.

config.note: There is no configuration file or published floorplan. The extracted experiment has an empty floorplan and empty power_w while still being labeled custom_2d_steady with steady_2d_relevant true. This is inconsistent: no runnable config can be built from the paper without invented geometry. Any generated shelf coordinates and constant power rows would be illustrative assumptions, not published placement or transient traces.

data.note: The seven power labels (0.2, 0.2, 1, 3, 2, 2, 1 W) and seven temperature labels (46, 46.1, 51, 62, 57, 55, 49 C) come only from pdftotext of the Fig. 6 page. Neither set is visually verified. No label maps to a named block, so no block has same-scenario power. The 62 C maximum observable has no location and is not a validated result; the aggregation is an inference. No power time series exists.

findings.reason: Fig. 6 is a schematic with no block names, coordinates, dimensions or power-to-block mapping. The extraction leaves floorplan and power_w empty but keeps kind=custom_2d_steady and steady_2d_relevant=true. No 2D reproduction target exists.

All power and temperature labels were read from pdftotext, not from the rendered figure. Label placement and the label-to-block association are unverified. Since the figure is the decisive evidence, no visual verification is supplied.
Taking the maximum of the seven labels (62 C) as the observable is an unsupported inference. The paper states no aggregation, location or validation for it.

The extraction says HotSpot is solved 'as a steady-state RC circuit' for the example. The survey only says the differential equations are solved with Runge-Kutta of order 4, and never mentions a steady-state solver for Fig. 6.
The 0.8 K/W value and 45 C ambient are general HotSpot or original-validation values. They are correctly flagged as not tied to Fig. 6, so they must not be used as parameters for the example.
The packet has no pinned assets and the paper links no repositories, so no code, config or data excerpt can be checked.
